Client Types

Public Clients

A public client is one without a method of securely storing any credentials. The most common example of this is an application that runs on the user's desktop. These clients:

  • Must only use the Authorization Code (with PKCE) grant type and must use a local redirect URI (ie. http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback).
  • Cannot use any service:* scopes.
  • Have access tokens that last for 10 hours and refresh tokens that last for 7 days.

Available Scopes

  • account:profile - for access to the account's basic profile information.
  • account:characters - for viewing the account's characters and inventories.
GET /oauth/authorize?client_id=example
&redirect_uri=https://example.com
